In your Introduction and \"The Most Ethical Path\" section, you skillfully linked real-world cases—such as the NHS HSSIB investigation—to patient harm and engineering obligations. To improve, broaden your recommendations to address multiple stakeholders, establish explicit threshold criteria for permissible shipping, and incorporate supporting visual elements such as summary tables or decision flowcharts.","next_steps":["In your recommendations, formulate distinct guidance for all key stakeholders (such as executive management, the contractor, and the health department) rather than focusing solely on Rachel.","Establish clear, risk-based threshold criteria defining when, if ever, products with minor non-critical defects may ethically be shipped.","Integrate visual elements, such as an ethical decision-making flowchart, stakeholder matrix, or risk table, to support and synthesize your discussion."],"criteria":{"C1":"Your \"INTRODUCTION\" clearly identified the ethical dilemma, grounding it effectively in engineering design and organizational pressures. You successfully outlined key stakeholders, including the chip contractor and healthcare recipients, demonstrating a comprehensive understanding of both organizational context and stakeholder interests. Keep up this thorough approach to problem framing.","C2":"In \"The Most Ethical Path\" and \"DICUSSION\", you provided objective arguments for and against shipping. To reach Excellent, expand your decision-making conclusions beyond Rachel and her company to provide tailored, actionable recommendations for several different stakeholders, such as client leadership, suppliers, and regulatory bodies.","C3":"Your report built a compelling, logical argument by using the NHS IT failure in \"The Most Ethical Path\" to connect data loss directly to patient harm. To achieve Excellent, ensure your arguments demonstrate a systematic understanding of the ethical issues across all identified stakeholders, fully linking their competing interests to your final conclusion.","C4":"You effectively supported your claims using reputable qualitative evidence, such as the NHS HSSIB case, the Volkswagen scandal, and the Engineers Australia Code of Ethics. To achieve Excellent, balance this qualitative research with quantitative evidence, such as defect rates, financial cost analyses, or statistical risks of server downtime.","C5":"Your writing was fluent, clear, and well-referenced from the \"ABSTRACT\" onward. However, the report lacked visual elements. To reach Very good or Excellent, incorporate relevant figures or tables (e.g., a risk matrix or stakeholder map) and proofread section headings carefully (e.g., correct \"DICUSSION\")."}}
